# landing/ — marketing page

A static page: React 18 UMD with in-browser Babel, and no build step. Preview it with the `landing` entry in `.claude/launch.json`, which runs `dev_server.py`.

- **A plain reload can run stale `.jsx`.** In-browser Babel fetches it through the HTTP cache. Before reloading, run `fetch(url, {cache: 'reload'})` on each changed file.
- **On narrow screens the replay is pinned under the nav, and the layer follows the scroll.** Each step is at least as tall as the screen left below the replay (`--pin-h`, measured in `app/app.jsx`), so wherever the page stops on a step its text is readable. This works only because phones scroll freely; don't add snapping back.
- **The replay's canvas must not change size except on a real resize.** Each resize reallocates the canvas and rescales the fighters. So on narrow screens, size things in `svh` rather than `dvh` (the URL bar changes `dvh`), and fade the log instead of collapsing it.
- **Every claim must match what the code does today.** Don't add accuracy, latency or throughput figures, and don't describe a live mode as shipped. The owner chose facts over marketing numbers.
- **`app/data.js` is real pipeline data.** `export_data.py` generates it; run `ai/.venv/bin/python landing/export_data.py` from the repo root. Never hand-edit it. It holds keypoints only and no video frames, because the fight footage isn't ours to publish.
- **Red and blue always mean corners, and orange is only the brand and CTA colour**, so a strike mark never reads as a corner.
- **Token values in `app/site.css` mirror `frontend/src/index.css`**, so the page and the app look like one product. That means a flat `--bg` (no grain, no glow orbs), no glow shadows, and the app's corner blue `#60a5fa`, which `CORNER` in `app/stage.jsx` repeats for the canvas. When an app token changes, change it here too.
- **The call to action is the waitlist** (`WaitlistForm` in `app/app.jsx`), because sign-in is invite-only. Sign-in stays as a quieter link for people already invited. Never offer uploading: it's admin-only.
- **The form posts to its own origin, `/api/auth/waitlist`.** In production Caddy forwards that one path from the landing host to the backend (`deploy/Caddyfile`); locally `dev_server.py` does the same, so start the backend to submit. Don't call the app's hostname from the page: that would need CORS on the backend.
- **Never send the email address to analytics.** The `waitlist` event carries only `from`.
- **With a mouse, trackpad or keyboard, each scroll moves exactly one section.** `app/pager.js` does this, reading its stops from each element's `scroll-snap-align` in `app/site.css`, so a new section needs one; without it, the pager jumps straight past the section. The mobile layout (up to 899px wide) and touch screens scroll freely, with no snapping and no pager. Mandatory snapping kept stopping mid-section on phones, so don't turn on `scroll-snap-type` for them. The pager checks width as well as touch because DevTools device mode doesn't always emulate touch.
- **Analytics is Umami Cloud's free plan and must stay cookieless.** The owner won't show a consent banner, so never add GA, Clarity, session replay or anything else that sets cookies. Each stored event property counts against the monthly event cap, so keep properties to one per event. The website ID is in `index.html`, and the script doesn't load on localhost.
- **The `<noscript>` block in `index.html` repeats the page's copy for crawlers and readers without JavaScript**, which otherwise see an empty `#root`. When copy in `app/app.jsx` changes, change it there too, and keep `APP_URL` in step with its sign-in link.
- **SEO URLs are absolute and name the landing host**, `https://fightlytics.duckdns.org/`: canonical, Open Graph, JSON-LD, `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`. Change them all together when the hostname changes, because a canonical that points at another host deindexes this one.
- **Caddy publishes only an allowlist of paths** (`@private` in `deploy/Caddyfile`). A new file at the landing root, like `robots.txt` or `og.png`, 404s in production until it's added there.
- **`og.png` and `apple-touch-icon.png` are drawn by `make_images.html`** from the page's fonts and `app/data.js`. Regenerate them there after a copy or brand change; don't edit the PNGs by hand.

fightlytics Back to home
Last updated 19 October 2026

Privacy.

Fightlytics is a free-time project, not a company. This page explains what it collects, why, where it’s kept, and how to get it deleted. The short version: only what’s needed to run the waitlist and the app. No ads, no selling data, and your fight videos are never used for training unless you say yes.

On this page At a glance What we collect Why, and legal basis Fight videos Who handles it How long we keep it Your rights Cookies Age Changes Contact
WaitlistYour email address, and whether you ticked monthly updates.
AccountYour name, email and profile picture from Google sign-in. No passwords stored.
VideosPrivate to you. Kept until you delete them. Used for training only if you opt in.
WhereServers in the EU. Analytics are cookieless and don’t identify you.
01

What we collect.

  • Waitlist: email address, signup date, and your monthly-updates choice.
  • Account: when you sign in with Google, we receive your name, email address and profile picture. Google handles your password; we never see it.
  • Your content: fight videos you upload, and the analyses, labels and notes created from them.
  • Technical data: IP address and browser details in server logs, kept briefly for security.
  • Usage statistics: anonymous page views via Umami. No cookies, and no way to tell who you are.
02

Why, and legal basis.

Under the GDPR, every use of your data needs a legal basis. Here’s ours:

PurposeLegal basis
Waitlist and invite emailsSteps you asked us to take before using the service (Art. 6(1)(b))
Running your account and analysing your videosProviding the service you signed up for (Art. 6(1)(b))
Monthly product updatesYour consent (Art. 6(1)(a)). Unsubscribe from any email.
Improving models with your videosYour consent (Art. 6(1)(a)). Off unless you turn it on.
Security logs and anonymous statisticsLegitimate interest in keeping the site safe and working (Art. 6(1)(f))
03

Fight videos.

Videos and analyses are private to your account. There’s no sharing or public profile.

We use them only to produce your analysis. If you turn on “Help improve Fightlytics”, your videos and labels may also be used to train our detection models. You can turn it off any time; future training then excludes your data.

Videos often show other people. Only upload footage you have the right to use. If you appear in a video someone else uploaded and want it removed, contact us.

04

Who handles it.

We don’t sell or share your data. These services process it on our behalf:

ServiceWhat it does
Oracle CloudHosts the app, database, videos and our own email server. EU region.
GoogleSign-in. Google’s own privacy policy applies to your Google account.
Umami CloudAnonymous, cookieless page statistics.

Emails are sent from our own mail server, not a third-party newsletter tool.

05

How long we keep it.

  • Waitlist email: until you unsubscribe or ask us to delete it.
  • Account data: until you close your account.
  • Videos and analyses: until you delete them, or close your account.
  • Server logs: a short period for security, then deleted.

If the project shuts down, everything is deleted.

06

Your rights.

You can ask to see, correct, delete or download your data, to restrict or object to how it’s used, and to withdraw consent at any time. Email us and we’ll reply within 30 days.

If you’re unhappy with how we handle your data, you can complain to the data protection authority in your EU country.

07

Cookies.

We set one essential cookie to keep you signed in. No tracking or advertising cookies, so there’s no cookie banner.

08

Age.

There’s no minimum age to use Fightlytics. If you’re under 16 (or your country’s age of digital consent), ask a parent or guardian before signing up or uploading videos.

09

Changes.

If this page changes in a way that matters, we’ll update the date at the top and email account holders before it takes effect.

Questions or requests?Write to us and a real person will answer.

filip.culig@gmail.com
© 2026 Fightlytics

I've built the design's privacy page as a static page at `landing/privacy.html`, with its styles in `landing/app/privacy.css`. It's plain HTML with no React or Babel, so it reads fine without JavaScript. I rendered it at 1440px and 390px wide and both layouts match the design: the table of contents sticks on desktop and is hidden on mobile, and the "At a glance" grid stacks into one column on mobile. Nothing is committed and nothing is deployed.

**How it differs from the design:**
- It uses the landing page's own colours, nav and footer from `app/site.css` instead of the design's `brand.css`, so it looks like the rest of the landing site.
- The design's "Back to app" button pointed at the app's sign-in page. I changed it to "Back to home" and pointed it at the landing page.
- It loads the same cookieless Umami analytics as `index.html`. The policy itself says page views are counted with Umami.

**To make it reachable, I also changed:**
- `deploy/Caddyfile`: added `/privacy.html` to the list of public paths. Without it the page would 404 in production.
- `landing/app/app.jsx`: added a "Privacy" link to the footer.
- `landing/index.html`: added the same link to the no-JavaScript fallback copy.
- `landing/sitemap.xml`: added an entry for the page.

**Before you push to `release`:** I kept the design's text word for word, but several claims don't match what the code does today. `landing/CLAUDE.md` says every claim on the site has to match the code, and here it's a legal statement, so this matters more than usual:

| Claim on the page | What the code does |
|---|---|
| Waitlist stores your "monthly-updates choice" | The `waitlist` table holds only `email` and `created_at`, and the form has no checkbox. |
